note: The feature backlog. Maintained by the team and AI agents. The owner's picks live in feature_choices.json, never here.

milestones.name: First slice
milestones.about: One city block that proves the whole loop.

milestones.name: Life depth
milestones.about: Careers, property, weather and a fuller town.

milestones.name: Full game

effort.note: Rough size of the extra work to reach a level from the one below. Estimates, not measurements.

features.title: City layout
features.why: How much city there is to walk around.

levels.name: One block
levels.what: One hand-built city block with streets around it.

levels.name: A district
levels.what: Several blocks laid out from lot data, loaded as you move.

levels.name: Whole city
levels.what: Districts with their own character, streamed seamlessly.

features.title: Lots and building records
features.why: Every plot knows what it is, who owns it and when it is open.

levels.name: Hand-placed
levels.what: Buildings are placed by hand with no data behind them.

levels.name: Registry
levels.what: A data record per lot drives signs, opening hours, owners and who lives or works there.

levels.name: Changing lots
levels.what: Lots can change use, be built on or stand empty over time.

features.title: Going inside buildings
features.why: Whether doors lead anywhere.

levels.name: Fronts only
levels.what: Buildings are fronts; people step in and vanish.

levels.name: Key rooms
levels.what: A few important buildings have one room you can enter.

levels.name: Most buildings
levels.what: Most buildings have furnished interiors.

levels.name: Every floor, true size
levels.what: Every building can be entered and every storey reached by its own stairs (and lifts in the towers). Inside is the same size as outside, behind the same windows; each floor is laid out and furnished for what it is (bedrooms upstairs in houses, a flat on each tower floor, offices, shop stores and staff rooms). Floors are built only near the player.

features.title: Building designer
features.why: Players make a place their own: remodel what they own, or build new on an open plot, in the town's look.

levels.name: None
levels.what: Buildings are as the town made them.

levels.name: Remodel
levels.what: Change the finishes of a building or unit you own: walls and their colour, brick or stone, roof tiles, windows and doors outside; floors, walls and ceilings inside. Every building is a design in data; choices from priced catalogues within the district's palette; checked, paid through the ledger.

levels.name: Build new
levels.what: On an empty plot: draw the footprint, set the storeys and each one's height, choose facades, roof, openings, stairs and lift, rooms and finishes; checked for planning, reachability, stairs and rooms; the result joins the estate market.

levels.name: Free-form and published
levels.what: L-shapes, courtyards, set-backs, bays and arcades; designs saved as templates and published by creators.

features.title: Open plots
features.why: Somewhere to build: the town is full today.

levels.name: None
levels.what: Every lot is built on.

levels.name: Plots for sale
levels.what: A few empty plots with an owner and a price, bought and sold through the estate market.

levels.name: Clear and rebuild
levels.what: Owners of a whole building may clear it (tenants given notice); plots come up over time.

features.title: From design to building
features.why: Building should take a little time and show in the street.

levels.name: Instant
levels.what: A confirmed design is there at once.

levels.name: Takes days
levels.what: Hoardings and scaffolding, then the building, over game days by its size; worked out from the clock.

levels.name: Builders at work
levels.what: Resident builders on site in their day, materials by van, stages you can watch.

features.title: Shops and market
features.why: Where money gets spent.

levels.name: Decoration
levels.what: Stalls and shop fronts you cannot use.

levels.name: Buy at a counter
levels.what: A shopkeeper sells a short list of goods through the ledger.

levels.name: Stock and prices
levels.what: Shops hold stock that sells down through the day and restocks, prices move with stock within set bounds, the player sells back to them, and the player can rent a market stall and sell to residents.

features.title: Mall
features.why: A big indoor place to shop and meet.

levels.name: None
levels.what: No mall; shops are on the street.

levels.name: Arcade
levels.what: One covered arcade with four shops and seating.

levels.name: Full mall
levels.what: Several floors, many shops, events and crowds.

features.title: Hospital and clinic
features.why: Where health is restored.

levels.name: A door
levels.what: A clinic front you cannot enter.

levels.name: Clinic room
levels.what: One room where a nurse restores health for a fee.

levels.name: Hospital
levels.what: A staffed hospital with wards, a medical career and an ambulance.

features.title: Bank, showroom, library, museum, cinema
features.why: Places for errands and evenings out beyond shops and cafes, and where money, cars and culture will later live.

levels.name: None
levels.what: No such places; the town has shops, cafes, a mall and a hospital.

levels.name: Places to visit
levels.what: A bank, a car showroom, a library, a museum and a cinema (plus a second hospital and mall), each with its own front and furnished interior, staff at work and residents visiting in their day.

levels.name: Working places
levels.what: They work: accounts and loans at the bank through the ledger, buying a car at the showroom, films on a timetable, exhibitions that change.

features.title: Workplaces
features.why: Where careers happen.

levels.name: Fronts
levels.what: Offices and workshops are fronts; workers go in and out.

levels.name: One job site

levels.name: Several careers
levels.what: Different workplaces for each career track.

features.title: Utility areas
features.why: Power, water, waste and depots.

levels.name: Set dressing
levels.what: A depot and pipes as scenery.

levels.name: Bills and workers
levels.what: Utility workers do rounds; lots get utility bills.

levels.name: Outages and repairs
levels.what: Things break; districts feel it; repair is a job.

features.title: Gardens and parks
features.why: Green places to rest and meet.

levels.name: Static garden
levels.what: A garden with paths and plants that never change.

levels.name: Living garden
levels.what: Benches people use, seasonal plants, a gardener at work.

levels.name: Community garden
levels.what: Players plant and tend plots; garden events.

features.title: Street dressing
features.why: Squares, parks and streets that look lived in: things to look at, sit on and play on, and signs that say what each building is.

levels.name: None
levels.what: As now: lamps, benches, flowerbeds and one small fountain in each park, court and square.

levels.name: Dressed places
levels.what: Objects placed as data in the block files, drawn in the town's look: playgrounds in the four big parks (swings, slide, seesaw, sandpit, climbing frame), a statue and a grand fountain on the squares, a bandstand in one park; hanging signs, awnings, painted wall adverts and hoardings, window boxes on buildings; bollards, bins, post boxes, bicycle racks, planters, notice boards, a news kiosk and a telephone box along streets; crates, barrows and bunting at the market. They stand still and block the way where solid.

levels.name: Used and changing
levels.what: Children play on the swings, slide and seesaw; residents read notice boards and buy at the kiosk; posters and cinema boards change with what is on; bunting only on market days; decorations change with the season.

levels.name: A handful

levels.name: A neighbourhood
levels.what: 20 to 30 residents per block, each with a home, a role and a look.

levels.name: A crowd
levels.what: Hundreds across the city, with cheaper far-away versions.

levels.what: Each person stays in one place.

levels.name: By the clock
levels.what: Home, work, meals and leisure by the time of day, a little different each day.

levels.name: By their needs

features.title: Week and calendar

levels.name: Every day the same

levels.name: Weekdays and weekends
levels.what: Work days, rest days and market days differ.

levels.name: Festivals
levels.what: Holidays and seasonal events change the whole town.

levels.name: Always there
levels.what: Everyone is always loaded. Fine for one block.

levels.name: Placed by routine

levels.name: Distance tiers
levels.what: Full, simple and data-only versions by distance, within a server budget, for many players.

features.title: Talking with residents
features.why: What happens when you speak to someone.

levels.name: Greetings
levels.what: People say a line as you pass.

levels.name: Dialogue
levels.what: Conversations with choices and outcomes, standing or walking.

levels.name: Residents talk to each other
levels.what: People chat among themselves and news spreads.

features.why: Whether a speaker's mouth and face move with what they say.

levels.name: Still faces
levels.what: The line shows as text; the face keeps its resting mouth.

levels.name: Talking mouth
levels.what: The speaker's mouth opens and closes in the rhythm of the line's text while it shows, and the face takes the line's mood.

levels.name: Lip sync
levels.what: Mouth shapes timed to each sound of the line (from its text, or from voice if Q-14 says so), expressions blended over time, nods and glances on stressed words.

features.title: Reacting to the world
features.why: Whether people notice rain, night and you.

levels.name: No reaction
levels.what: People ignore weather and time.

levels.name: Weather and night
levels.what: People dress for the weather (coats and hoods on cold or wet days, umbrellas up in rain), hurry for cover when rain starts and wait it out under awnings or indoors; lamps and windows light up; people glance at you.

levels.name: Events
levels.what: People gather, flee or help when something happens.

features.title: Getting out of the way of cars
features.why: Whether residents see a car coming at them and react like people would.

levels.name: Pushed aside
levels.what: A car that reaches a resident stops and the resident is pushed aside (CITY-064 as written).

levels.name: Dodge
levels.what: Residents see a car heading at them and scramble out of its path: a hurried sidestep or jump to the side, then carry on.

levels.name: Dodge and tell off
levels.what: Once clear, they turn on the driver: a raised fist or arms flung up and a short shout (a speech tag, no words spoken, Q-14), then go back to what they were doing.

features.title: Animals

levels.name: None
levels.what: No animals.

levels.name: Ambient

levels.name: Pets

levels.name: Shared

levels.name: Nothing moves

levels.name: Residents carry

levels.name: Things stay moved

levels.name: Real traffic

features.why: Public transport people ride.

levels.name: None
levels.what: No public transport.

levels.name: Network

features.title: Driving yourself

levels.name: Bicycle or scooter
levels.what: A light vehicle to own and ride.

levels.name: Cars
levels.what: Cars to buy, drive and park.

levels.name: Bump

levels.name: Broken until mended

levels.name: Plain sky

levels.name: Blue sky and drifting clouds

levels.name: Clouds follow the weather

features.title: Weather
features.why: Rain, cloud and fog shared by everyone.

levels.name: Always clear
levels.what: No weather.

levels.name: Changing weather
levels.what: Clear, cloud, rain and fog, the same for every player.

levels.name: Storms that matter
levels.what: Storms, puddles and effects on needs and trade.

features.title: Seasons
features.why: A year that turns.

levels.name: One season
levels.what: Always summer.

levels.name: Four seasons
levels.what: Light, weather odds and plants change through the year.

levels.name: Seasonal life
levels.what: Seasonal goods, prices and activities.

features.title: Plant and tree growth
features.why: Plants get bigger over the years.

levels.name: Static
levels.what: Plants never change size.

levels.name: Growth from age
levels.what: Size is worked out from how long ago something was planted.

levels.name: Planting and tending
levels.what: Players plant, water and harvest on land they own.

features.title: Spring, autumn and leaf fall
features.why: Buds, blossom, autumn colour and bare branches.

levels.name: Evergreen
levels.what: Leaves never change.

levels.name: Leaf cycle
levels.what: Each kind of tree buds, blossoms, turns and drops its leaves on its own dates.

levels.name: Leaves on the ground
levels.what: Fallen leaves pile up and are swept away by residents.

features.title: Trees falling and being replanted
features.why: Old or storm-hit trees come down and new ones go in.

levels.name: Trees are forever
levels.what: Nothing ever happens to a tree.

levels.name: Fall and replant
levels.what: Trees reach the end of their life, are cleared and replanted by the town.

levels.name: Storm damage
levels.what: Storms bring trees down across paths; clearing them is a job.

features.title: Sounds of the city
features.why: What you hear around you: engines, the tram, voices, birds, doors.

levels.name: Ambience bed
levels.what: One looping street ambience that changes with time of day and indoors or outdoors.

levels.name: Things make sound
levels.what: Each nearby car, tram, resident and door makes its own sound from where it is: engine pitch follows speed, the tram hums and rings its bell at stops, residents murmur when they talk (no words, Q-14), footsteps, birds by day.

levels.name: Full mix
levels.what: Sounds follow the world: rain and wind with the weather, echo indoors and in streets, a mix that stays clear in crowds, and each kind of building with its own room sound.

features.title: Interaction sounds
features.why: Feedback when you do something: open a door, sit, use an object, drive.

levels.name: Menu clicks
levels.what: Sounds for the interface only: prompts, choices, money in and out.

levels.name: Every action
levels.what: Every interaction point and the player car have their own sound: doors, chairs, taps, the car door, engine start, horn, skids.

levels.name: Made by creators
levels.what: Creators can attach their own sounds to items they make, checked like other user content.

features.title: Music
features.why: Mood, and music as something people play and listen to.

levels.name: Background score
levels.what: A soft score that changes with time of day; mutes in conversations.

levels.name: Music in the world
levels.what: Music comes from places: car radio with a few music stations and podcasts, shop and café music, a busker; the score fades when a source is near.

levels.name: Players make music
levels.what: Instruments and speakers players own and play for others, heard by everyone nearby.

features.title: Money and the bank
features.why: Brix in a ledger: what the player earns, keeps, saves and borrows.

levels.name: Cash only
levels.what: Cash in the player's pocket, moved only through the ledger; no bank account.

levels.name: One account
levels.what: Cash plus one current account at the bank, a statement of every movement.

levels.name: Full bank
levels.what: Current and savings accounts with interest each game day, loans with a schedule, late fees and repossession on default.

features.title: Quests from residents
features.why: Things to do for the people of the town, and money for doing them.

levels.name: None
levels.what: No quests; money comes from the job only.

levels.name: Starter quest lines
levels.what: A few short quest lines given in conversation, a quest log, rewards through the ledger, progress saved.

levels.name: Branching and repeatable
levels.what: Choices that branch a quest line to different endings, daily jobs offered by residents worked out from the day, reputation with each resident.

features.title: Character designer
features.why: Players make who they are before they walk into town.

levels.name: Default character
levels.what: Everyone starts as the same player character.

levels.name: Presets
levels.what: Choose from set options for body, skin, hair and outfit.

levels.name: Full designer
levels.what: Sliders for height, build and face shape, every skin tone, hair, garments, colours, extras and walk, with a live preview; stored as compact values.

features.title: Real estate market
features.why: Every building and every unit inside it is owned by someone (a player, a resident or a real estate company) and can be bought, sold and rented.

levels.name: Owners on record
levels.what: Every building and unit has an owner in the lot registry (resident, company or the city); For Sale and To Let signs show it. Nothing can be bought.

levels.name: Buy, sell and rent
levels.what: Buildings of every kind (homes, shops, workplaces, utilities) are split into units (flats, shop floors, offices). The player buys, sells and rents buildings or single units through the ledger, from residents and from several real estate companies that each hold a portfolio and an account. Prices come from data: size, kind, block and condition. Mortgages from the bank. Buying and selling carry a transfer tax and agent fee (sinks); owners pay upkeep and tax each day, tenants pay rent. Settled from the clock, not ticked.

levels.name: Living market
levels.what: Companies buy, sell, list and set rents on their own from demand (empty units, residents moving, nearby shops), so prices and rents rise and fall within data bounds per block. Residents buy and move house. Players compete with companies and each other; a price index and the money supply are published and kept balanced by tuned faucets and sinks.

features.title: Furniture that belongs to the unit
features.why: Furniture is part of the home: sell the flat and its furniture goes with it, unless the owner takes it out first.

levels.name: Fixed furnishing
levels.what: Units come furnished; the furniture is part of the unit and is sold with it. It cannot be moved.

levels.name: Owned, placed from the inventory, sold with the unit
levels.what: Each piece of furniture is an owned item. Bought or taken out, it sits in the player's inventory; the player places it in a unit they own or rent, and once placed it is recorded against that unit. A sale or repossession of the unit includes everything still in it, and its value counts toward the price. The player can pick a placed piece back up into the inventory. Storage containers are a separate feature (F-PROP-STORAGE).

levels.name: Arrange and trade
levels.what: The owner places, moves and turns furniture freely inside the unit (PROP-003), buys it from furniture shops and sells it on; furniture wears and has its own price. Visitors see the layout.

features.title: Storage containers
features.why: Somewhere to keep furniture and belongings that are not in use, so the inventory does not have to hold everything.

levels.name: None
levels.what: No storage; furniture is either placed in a home or held in the inventory.

levels.name: Locker and storage unit
levels.what: The player moves pieces from the inventory or a home into a locker (small, free) or a rented storage unit at a storage depot (sized, rent each day through the ledger, settled from the clock), and takes them out again into the inventory.

levels.name: Containers everywhere
levels.what: Wardrobes, chests, cupboards and shelves in a home hold items by size; storage units of several sizes at more than one depot; unpaid rent ends in the contents being sold at auction.

features.title: Furniture designs
features.why: Homes, shops and offices need furniture, and a large catalogue needs many pieces that still look like one world.

levels.name: Basic set
levels.what: About 30 plain pieces (bed, sofa, table, chairs, desk, wardrobe, shelves, lamp, kitchen run, bath) in one style, used to dress interiors. Made in Blender to the locked look; an interior style section is added to ART_DIRECTION first, with the owner's approval.

levels.name: Kit and variants
levels.what: About 80 base pieces built from one shared kit (legs, frames, cushions, handles) on a common grid, each with finishes and colours set in data, giving about 400 catalogue items in four style lines (budget, modern, classic, retro). A Blender look test renders every piece to check it matches the reference.

levels.name: Large range
levels.what: About 200 base pieces and 1,500+ catalogue items across every room (living, bed, kitchen, bath, children, office, garden, shop fittings), with seasonal collections added from data, wear that shows with age, and sets that match across a room.

features.title: Furniture company and outlets
features.why: Somewhere to see furniture full size, laid out in rooms, before buying it, and a company that sells it through the ledger.

levels.name: Outlet to walk round
levels.what: One huge furniture outlet on the edge of town: a big shed with a car park, a showroom floor of furnished room sets, a marked walking route, a café and a warehouse hall. Residents browse it in their day. Nothing can be bought.

levels.name: See it, buy it, have it delivered
levels.what: A furniture company with its own account and catalogue (data). Every piece on the showroom floor carries a tag with name, price and the catalogue's other colours; the catalogue can also be browsed at the outlet or at home. The player buys at the till through the ledger and the piece is owned (PROP-001). At the till the player chooses delivery or instant. Delivery: on a booked slot a crew of the company's workers (residents) drives a van to the building, unloads and carries each piece through the door and up the stairs or lift into the flat, flat-packed in its boxes or assembled, as chosen at the till. A flat-packed piece stays boxed in the flat until it is put together: either the player assembles it (a timed action in this level) or pays the company for assembly, and a fitter assembles it in place. Instant: the piece goes straight into the player's inventory, at no extra cost (free for now; the charge, if any, is a tunable number in data). From the inventory the player places it in a home (F-PROP-FURNISH) or, later, moves it to storage (F-PROP-STORAGE).

levels.name: Several companies, living catalogue
levels.what: Three companies (a budget flat-pack chain, a mid-range chain and a premium design house) with outlets of different sizes, two of them huge. Catalogues change with the seasons; sales and ex-display clearance; stock and delivery slots per day calculated from the clock, so delivery dates move when vans are busy; delivery crews and vans in traffic; residents buy furniture and get it delivered too; the player can sell used furniture back or on the market stall.

features.title: Assembling flat-pack furniture
features.why: Putting furniture together from the instructions is a small, satisfying job of its own.

levels.name: Timed action
levels.what: The player assembles a boxed piece with one action that takes a set time from data; the boxes turn into the piece.

levels.name: Follow the instructions
levels.what: A mini-game: the boxes open into labelled parts and fixings, and the player follows the instruction sheet step by step to fit them together. Mistakes show (a wobble, a part left over) and can be undone.

levels.name: Every piece its own build
levels.what: Every flat-pack piece in the catalogue has its own steps made from data; help from a friend makes it faster in multiplayer; a well-built piece wears more slowly.

features.title: The game menu
features.why: One place for everything about the player's life (money, belongings, homes, quests, the map, saving) instead of a key for each, and a way into the building designer from what you own.

levels.name: Keys only
levels.what: As now: a key for each panel (I money, J quests, P property, M map) and the keys listed along the bottom of the screen.

levels.name: Menu of what exists
levels.what: The platform's menu control (Esc on a keyboard, Start or Menu on a gamepad, a menu button on touch) opens a menu over the dimmed game with tabs: Money, Journal, Properties (with Show on map, Remodel, Furnish, Sell and Let buttons), Map, Save (save now, last autosave, load, new game) and Help (the controls of the platform played on, which leave the bottom of the screen). The old shortcuts open their tab.

levels.name: Every tab
levels.what: Also Me (name, look, job, standing with residents and shops), Wardrobe, Belongings, Storage and Settings; the map with filters and a waypoint; more than one save slot.

features.title: Settings
features.why: Players set the game to their machine and their taste: picture, sound, controls, what the screen shows. Settings belong to the device, not the save; their defaults are data. Controls follow the platform: keyboard and mouse, a gamepad, or touch each have their own mapping.

levels.name: Keys only
levels.what: As now: O for the better or simple picture, N for sound; nothing else can be set.

levels.name: Picture, sound, display, mouse
levels.what: Graphics: one switch for the better or simple picture and, under it, shadows, ambient occlusion, bounce light, contact shade and resolution; view distance, how many people have full bodies, field of view, the frame counter. Audio: master, music, street, voices, interface. Display: minimap, clock, money, names over residents, prompts, text size. Controls for the platform played on (keyboard and mouse, gamepad, touch), each with its own default mapping in data: sensitivity, invert, camera distance, first or third person; the Help tab shows that platform's controls. Kept on the device; defaults in World/rules/settings.json.

levels.name: Controls and accessibility
levels.what: Also remapping every action, per platform (keys, gamepad buttons; touch layouts); colour-blind-safe markers, reduced motion (no camera glides), hold or toggle; hints on or off; the starting clock speed.

features.title: Belongings
features.why: Everything the player owns that is not placed or stored in one list: what they carry and furniture waiting to be placed (FURN-050).

levels.name: Carried items only
levels.what: As now: the wallet panel lists the shop items the player carries.

levels.name: One list of belongings
levels.what: Carried items and unplaced furniture together, by kind, with what each is worth; furniture taken away in the designer goes here and is placed from here.

levels.name: Use, drop and limits
levels.what: Items can be used, given, dropped or sold from the list; how much can be carried is limited by size and weight; the rest must be stored or placed.

features.title: Wardrobe and outfits
features.why: Players change how they look after the character designer: clothes for the day, the season and the occasion.

levels.name: Fixed look
levels.what: As now: the look made in the character designer is kept for good.

levels.name: Saved outfits
levels.what: The player saves looks from the character designer's own choices (garments, colours, extras, hair) as named outfits and changes between them, free, from the menu.

levels.name: Clothes you own
levels.what: Garments are owned items bought in clothes shops through the ledger and kept in a wardrobe at home; you change at a wardrobe, a fitting room or home; clothes suit the weather (CITY-077 to CITY-080).
